title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is part of Grothendieck's notes from the Barsotti-Tate/crystal period (about 1970-72). The neighbouring pages in the photocopied folder are unrelated, apparently Bourbaki-style Banach algebra exercises.

(1) The pencilled margin gives polygon inequalities between two families of slopes λ'_j and λ_j: the partial sums satisfy Σ_1^i λ'_j ≤ Σ_1^i λ_j, with equality of the total sums. The margin note reads 'pentes de Hodge', and there is also a sum Σ i h_i'. This is the standard form of a polygon comparison with equal endpoints. Examples are Mazur's inequality (the Hodge polygon lies below the Newton polygon) and Grothendieck's specialization theorem for Newton polygons (they rise under specialization). Here it is attached to Hodge slopes h_i.

(2) Main text. It quotes Tate's theorem (Driebergen 1966, published 1967). Let S be a noetherian, normal, integral scheme whose generic point η has residue field of characteristic 0. Then restriction BT(S) → BT(η) of Barsotti-Tate (p-divisible) groups is fully faithful. So a BT group over S is determined, up to unique isomorphism, by its p-adic Galois representation of π_1(η) = Gal(k(η)^sep/k(η)).

Specialising to S = Spec V, with V a complete DVR of mixed characteristic and perfect residue field k, Grothendieck poses two questions:
- (a) Characterise the Galois modules that arise. Tate's necessary condition is that they be of Hodge-Tate type.
- (b) Give an explicit functor from these Galois modules to F-crystals M over k, equipped with a filtration on M⊗_W V.

(3) 'Problème'. Tate's theorem suggests that the 'mysterious functor' from F-crystals over k filtered over L to Galois Q_p-modules over L is fully faithful. One should then be able to make explicit a quasi-inverse defined on a suitable full subcategory of Galois Q_p-representations, presumably contained in the Hodge-Tate ones. In modern terms this is exactly Fontaine's programme: D_cris and V_cris built from B_cris, crystalline representations as a full subcategory of the de Rham and Hodge-Tate ones, and the equivalence with weakly admissible filtered φ-modules (Colmez-Fontaine 2000).

(4) Conjecture. The hypothesis that k(η) = L has characteristic 0 in Tate's theorem should be unnecessary. The next page reduces the remaining case, where L has characteristic p, to two inputs:
- Dieudonné theory over perfect rings, giving an equivalence of categories.
- Full faithfulness of restriction to the generic point for locally free crystals, or at least F-crystals, over a normal noetherian integral S of characteristic p. This reduces to S = Spec k[[t]] and becomes a statement about modules with formal connection.

This is the equal-characteristic Tate conjecture for p-divisible groups. It was proved by de Jong: first over DVRs ('Crystalline Dieudonné module theory via formal and rigid geometry', Publ. IHÉS 82, 1995), then in general (Invent. Math. 134, 1998). The proof passes through full faithfulness for Dieudonné crystals and F-crystals, close to the strategy outlined here. Related full-faithfulness results for F-isocrystals were later proved by Kedlaya (2004).
errors: No mathematical errors. Tate's theorem is stated correctly: normal noetherian integral base with characteristic-0 function field. Tate's own statement is for integrally closed noetherian domains.
Minor imprecision: π_1(η) = Gal(k(η)^bar/k(η)) should strictly use the separable closure. This only matters in the characteristic-p case contemplated at the end of the page.

In (b) and in the 'Problème' the directions of the functors are loose. The mysterious functor goes from filtered F-crystals to Galois modules, and the requested 'explicit functor' in (b) goes the other way. Fontaine later realised both directions (V_cris and D_cris), so the speculation is consistent but not precise.

missed.claim: The page documents the reduction strategy for the equal-characteristic Tate theorem in an early private draft: full faithfulness of Cris(S) → Cris(η) for F-crystals, reduced to k[[t]] and formal connections, plus Dieudonné theory over perfect rings. This is essentially the route de Jong later followed. It is of historical interest but not new mathematics.
missed.quote: si on sait faire la théorie de Dieudonné sur un anneau parfait (avec équivalence de catégories alors on aura démonstration du th. de Tate en égales car.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only historical: it dates Grothendieck's anticipation of the de Jong strategy. The results are all now proved and the problems are known to be his.

deep.surprise_reason: These are draft notes of material Grothendieck made public at ICM 1970 and in the Montréal notes: the mysterious functor, the Hodge-Tate subcategory guess, and the equal-characteristic conjecture. Fontaine and de Jong later resolved them along essentially the indicated lines. The only mild interest is seeing the explicit proof strategy for the characteristic-p case in an early draft.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription gives the marginal pencil note as 'pentes [?] de Hodge [?]'; it plausibly reads 'pentes de Hodge', or perhaps 'suite des pentes de Hodge'.
'Driebergen' is the typed spelling. It refers to the 1966 Driebergen conference (Proceedings of a Conference on Local Fields).
In the definition of π_1(η), the overline is over k(η) (algebraic closure), as typed.
In (b), 'M⊗_W V' is typed with V overstruck, apparently a correction from another letter to V.
